items.title: First flight, 120 feet in 12 seconds, 10:35 a.m.; Kitty Hawk, North Carolina
items.depicts: THE photograph. The 1903 Wright Flyer a few feet above the sand, flying left to right; Orville lying prone on the lower wing at the controls; Wilbur standing on the right, in a dark suit and cap, having let go of the wing. The launching rail runs diagonally in the left foreground, with the wooden wing-rest bench in the centre; a coil box, a can and other gear lie on the sand at right. Flat grey sky, distant dunes. Plate damage: a broken-off glass corner (white) at bottom left, a ghosted figure at the far left edge, small dark spots at the bottom.
items.evidence: LoC item 00652085 record: title "[First flight, 120 feet in 12 seconds, 10:35 a.m.; Kitty Hawk, North Carolina]"; created "[1903 Dec. 17]"; contributors "Wright, Wilbur ... Wright, Orville ... Daniels, John T., photographer"; summary: "Photograph shows the first powered, controlled, sustained flight. Orville Wright at the controls of the machine, lying prone on the lower wing ... Wilbur Wright running alongside to balance the machine, has just released his hold on the forward upright of the right wing. The starting rail, the wing-rest, a coil box, and other items ... are visible ... (Orville Wright preset the camera and had John T. Daniels squeeze the rubber bulb, tripping the shutter.)" Medium: glass negative, dry plate, 5x7. Reproduction no. LC-DIG-ppprs-00626 (digital file from original); call no. LC-W86-35. Viewed at full res: it matches the record. Note that LoC's 'Kitty Hawk' means the Kill Devil Hills site near Kitty Hawk.

items.title: Wilbur Wright, age 38, head and shoulders, about 1905; one of the earliest published photographs of him
items.depicts: Portrait of Wilbur Wright, half length, facing the camera with a direct gaze: bald crown, high white collar, dark patterned tie, dark single-breasted pinstripe jacket, against a plain black backdrop. The face is sharp and clean. Emulsion flaking runs down the right edge and across the top edge of the plate, with a small mark near the bottom of the jacket.

items.title: Orville Wright, age 34, head and shoulders, with mustache
items.depicts: Portrait of Orville Wright, head and shoulders, three-quarter view looking slightly to the viewer's right: full dark mustache, parted dark hair, high white collar, striped tie, dark jacket and waistcoat, against a black backdrop. The face is clean and sharp. Heavy emulsion loss forms a ragged black border all around the plate edges; crop inside it, or use it as a period vignette.

items.title: Orville making right turn, showing warping of wings, hill visible in front of him; Kitty Hawk, North Carolina
items.depicts: The 1902 glider (unpowered) banking low over the sand from the left, its wings visibly warped and slightly motion-blurred, the pilot prone at the centre. Big sand hills fill the background; the foreground is rippled sand with footprints. The plate is clean apart from a few dark specks and a dark strip at the right edge. Wide and calm, good for a slow push-in.
items.evidence: LoC item 2001696262 record: title "[Orville making right turn, showing warping of wings, hill visible in front of him; Kitty Hawk, North Carolina]"; created "[1902 Oct. 24]"; medium "1 negative : glass, dry plate ; 5 x 7 in."; reproduction no. LC-DIG-ppprs-00599 (digital file from original); call no. LC-W86-8. This is a 1902 GLIDER, not the 1903 powered Flyer.

items.title: Wilbur gliding in level flight, single rear rudder clearly visible; Kitty Hawk, North Carolina
items.depicts: The 1902 glider in level flight against a pale sky, seen from slightly below and to the side: biplane wings, struts and wire bracing, the single vertical rear rudder at the right, and Wilbur prone on the lower wing. A flat horizon of sand sits low in the frame. A large white area of emulsion loss covers the left third of the plate; the glider itself, in the right-centre, is untouched. Crop right of x≈0.33.

items.title: 1903 machine and large camp building where it was housed, and smaller building used as a workshop and living quarters at Kill Devil Hills
items.depicts: The 1903 Flyer standing on the sand at the left; to its right, the open-fronted wooden hangar with one man in a dark suit and hat standing in the doorway, then the smaller board-and-batten workshop/living shed. A wide empty sky fills the upper half and flat sand the lower. Vertical white masking strips run along the left and right edges of the plate, with a small stain at bottom left. Otherwise clean.

items.title: 1903 machine on the launching track at Big Kill Devil Hill, prior to the December 14th trial. Four men from the Kill Devil Hills Lifesaving Station helped move it from the shed to the hill, accompanied by two small boys and a dog
items.depicts: The 1903 Flyer resting on the slope of Big Kill Devil Hill, with its wooden launching track/rail running diagonally down toward the lower left. To its right stand four men in dark coats and caps (the lifesaving crew) and two small boys; a trestle and a box sit on the sand at right. A long bare dune slope and pale sky fill the background, with footprint trails in the foreground. The plate is very clean.
items.evidence: LoC item 2001696494 record: title "[1903 machine on the launching track at Big Kill Devil Hill, prior to the December 14th trial. Four men from the Kill Devil Hills Lifesaving Station helped move it from the shed to the hill, accompanied by two small boys and a dog]"; created "[1903 Dec. 14]"; reproduction no. LC-DIG-ppprs-00613 (digital file from original); call no. LC-W86-22. DO NOT caption as 17 December: this is 14 Dec 1903, before Wilbur's unsuccessful trial that day.

items.title: 1903 machine, front view
items.depicts: A dead-on frontal view of the 1903 Flyer on flat sand: a long, symmetrical biplane span, two twin pusher propellers angled in a V behind the wings, the engine and pilot cradle at the centre, and the skids resting on a low wooden rail/track. Pale sky, low dunes on the horizon. Emulsion damage at the right edge and a large dark blotch at bottom right; a thin wavy line on the sand in the foreground. A strong graphic, symmetrical frame.

items.title: O. & W. Wright, Flying Machine, US Patent No. 821,393: drawing sheet 1 of 3 (Fig. 1)
items.depicts: Black line-art patent sheet on white. The header reads "No. 821,393. PATENTED MAY 22, 1906. O. & W. WRIGHT. FLYING MACHINE. APPLICATION FILED MAR. 23, 1903. 3 SHEETS—SHEET 1." FIG. 1 is a large perspective drawing of the biplane machine (wing-warping cables, standards, forward horizontal rudder, rear vertical rudder), with numbered callouts, drawn on a diagonal down the page. At the bottom are the witness signatures (William F. Bauer, Irvine Miller), 'INVENTORS Orville Wright, Wilbur Wright' and the attorney's signature (H. A. Toulmin). The drawn machine is the unpowered glider configuration covered by the patent: no engine or propellers.
items.evidence: Google Patents US821393A: title 'Flying-machine.'; inventors Orville Wright, Wilbur Wright; priority/filing date 1903-03-23; publication date 1906-05-22. File is the full-size 'US821393-drawings-page-1.png' (2320x3408, 1-bit) that the page's metadata links to; converted losslessly to 8-bit greyscale PNG. The header text visible on the sheet confirms the patent number and dates.
